questions.stem: The Revolt of 1857 began at which cantonment on which date, over the issue of greased cartridges?

options.option_text: MEERUT, 10 May 1857 — later reached Delhi 11 May

questions.explanation: THE FULL-SCALE REVOLT began at MEERUT on 10 MAY 1857 — 85 sepoys of the 3rd Light Cavalry who refused to use the new cartridges on 24 April were court-martialled and sentenced to 10 years' hard labour. On 9 May, they were publicly humiliated (stripped of uniforms). On 10 May, fellow sepoys mutinied, released them, killed British officers + civilians. The next day (11 May), mutineers reached DELHI and proclaimed BAHADUR SHAH II ZAFAR (the last Mughal emperor) as Emperor of Hindustan. MANGAL PANDEY (34th Bengal Native Infantry) had attacked a British officer at BARRACKPORE on 29 March 1857 — he was hanged 8 April 1857. Though not the start of the revolt, he is considered its first martyr. The CARTRIDGE ISSUE: the new Enfield rifles required biting paper cartridges greased with BEEF (offending Hindus) + PORK (offending Muslims) — though other causes were deeper.

questions.stem: Match the 1857 Revolt centre to its leader:

options.option_text: Delhi — Bakht Khan; Kanpur — Nana Saheb + Tantia Tope; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal; Bihar — Kunwar Singh
Delhi — Rani Lakshmibai; Kanpur — Bahadur Shah
All centres led by Tantia Tope
All led by civilian leaders only

questions.explanation: 1857 Revolt — regional leaders: DELHI — Nominal: Bahadur Shah Zafar (last Mughal); Military: BAKHT KHAN (Rohilla commander). KANPUR (Cawnpore) — NANA SAHEB (adopted son of last Peshwa Baji Rao II, denied pension by Dalhousie); General: TANTIA TOPE (his most brilliant military leader). JHANSI — RANI LAKSHMIBAI (Manikarnika/Manu, adopted son's inheritance denied under Doctrine of Lapse) — died in combat 17 June 1858 at Gwalior. LUCKNOW — BEGUM HAZRAT MAHAL (on behalf of her minor son Birjis Qadr, the deposed Nawab of Awadh's heir). BIHAR — KUNWAR SINGH (80-year-old Rajput zamindar of Jagdishpur). FAIZABAD — MAULVI AHMADULLAH SHAH. BUNDELKHAND — RANI of Ramgarh (Awanti Bai). BAREILLY — KHAN BAHADUR KHAN. Most leaders were killed or captured within 1857-58. ONLY Nana Saheb's fate remains unknown — possibly escaped to Nepal.

questions.stem: The 1857 Revolt's IMMEDIATE trigger — the ENFIELD RIFLE cartridge issue — offended sepoys because:

options.option_text: Cartridges were made of cow's leather only
Cartridges were greased with COW + PIG fat, offending Hindus + Muslims respectively, requiring sepoys to BITE THE CARTRIDGE before loading

questions.explanation: ENFIELD RIFLE issued in 1853-56 required the user to BITE off the top of the paper cartridge before loading. The paper was greased to be water-resistant; rumour spread (likely true in some batches) that the grease was TALLOW (COW fat — offensive to Hindus, sacred cow) + LARD (PIG fat — haram for Muslims). This triggered sepoy refusal. While the cartridge issue was the IMMEDIATE trigger, DEEPER CAUSES included: (1) POLITICAL — Doctrine of Lapse (Dalhousie — annexed Jhansi, Nagpur, Satara, Awadh, etc. without heir), Subsidiary Alliance, annexation of Awadh 1856, pension cut-off to Nana Saheb; (2) ECONOMIC — Permanent Settlement caused zamindar-peasant distress; Indian artisans destroyed by British imports; heavy taxation; (3) SOCIAL/RELIGIOUS — abolition of sati (1829), widow remarriage (1856) seen as interference; missionary activity; (4) MILITARY — sepoy discrimination in pay, promotion, overseas postings (General Service Enlistment Act 1856 required overseas deployment, violating caste).

questions.stem: After the defeat of the 1857 Revolt, the BRITISH CROWN took DIRECT control from the East India Company via:
questions.explanation: GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ACT 1858: passed 2 August 1858 — formally ended East India Company rule; transferred all territories to the BRITISH CROWN. KEY CHANGES: (1) The office of GOVERNOR-GENERAL was retitled VICEROY (Lord Canning became first Viceroy, 1 Nov 1858); (2) Created the SECRETARY OF STATE FOR INDIA (first: Lord Stanley) — a UK cabinet minister responsible for India, assisted by a 15-member Council of India; (3) ABOLISHED Board of Control + Court of Directors (East India Company dissolved). QUEEN'S PROCLAMATION (1 November 1858, Allahabad, read by Canning) — Queen Victoria's declaration: (a) Promise of religious tolerance; (b) Respect for princely states' rights; (c) NO MORE annexations via Doctrine of Lapse; (d) Equal rights for all subjects, no racial discrimination (promised but rarely delivered); (e) Amnesty for most rebels. Queen Victoria took the title EMPRESS OF INDIA via ROYAL TITLES ACT 1876 (during Lord Lytton's viceroyalty). 1857 is sometimes called INDIA'S FIRST WAR OF INDEPENDENCE (V.D. Savarkar's 1909 book popularised this view, though many British historians call it 'Sepoy Mutiny'). + Queen's Proclamation, 1 Nov 1858.

questions.stem: 'DOCTRINE OF LAPSE' — a major cause of 1857 Revolt — was a policy by which British Governor-General?
questions.explanation: DOCTRINE OF LAPSE (1848) — introduced by LORD DALHOUSIE (Governor-General 1848-56). POLICY: if an Indian ruler died without a BIOLOGICAL MALE HEIR, his kingdom would LAPSE to (be annexed by) the British EIC. Traditional Indian practice of adopting an heir was disallowed. States annexed under this doctrine: SATARA (1848 — first, Maratha), JAITPUR (1849), SAMBALPUR (1849), BAGHAT (1850), UDAIPUR (1852), JHANSI (1853 — Rani Lakshmibai's adopted son Damodar Rao denied inheritance), NAGPUR (1854 — Bhonsles). AWADH annexed in 1856 NOT under Doctrine of Lapse but on grounds of 'MISGOVERNANCE' (even more resented since Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was a British ally). The Doctrine was FORMALLY REVOKED via the Queen's Proclamation 1858. Dalhousie's other actions: Railways 1853 (Bombay-Thana), Telegraph 1853 (Calcutta-Agra), Postal Service 1854, Wood's Despatch on Education 1854, Widow Remarriage Act 1856. Governor-General 1848-1856.

questions.stem: RANI LAKSHMIBAI of Jhansi — iconic heroine of 1857 — died in battle on which date at which location?
questions.explanation: RANI LAKSHMIBAI (born 19 Nov 1828 Varanasi as MANIKARNIKA 'Manu' Tambe) — married Raja Gangadhar Rao of Jhansi 1842, renamed Lakshmi Bai. Husband died 1853; adopted son Damodar Rao's succession was REJECTED by British under Doctrine of Lapse → Jhansi annexed 1854. Rani took charge during 1857 Revolt — held Jhansi fort against Sir Hugh Rose's siege (March-April 1858) — fell after bombardment. Fled with adopted son + small force → reached Kalpi → met TANTIA TOPE + NANA SAHEB's brother Rao Saheb → captured GWALIOR FORT (June 1858, ousted Scindia ruler who was pro-British). British (under Sir Hugh Rose + Sir Robert Hamilton) counter-attacked Gwalior. Rani died in battle on 17-18 JUNE 1858 at KOTAH-KI-SARAI near Gwalior — cut down fighting in male disguise, her body burnt by her own soldiers to prevent British desecration. Age 29. HUGH ROSE called her 'the best and bravest of rebel leaders'. MEMORIAL: Jhansi Fort today. Subhadra Kumari Chauhan's famous poem: 'Khoob Lari Mardani Wo To Jhansi Wali Rani Thi' ('She fought valiantly, she was the Rani of Jhansi').

questions.stem: Which of the following regions/groups did NOT participate actively in the 1857 Revolt?

options.option_text: Awadh (Oudh) — one of the major centres
Delhi — nominal leader Bahadur Shah Zafar
Punjab (Sikhs), South India, most Princely States — largely LOYAL to British

questions.explanation: GEOGRAPHIC LIMIT of 1857 REVOLT: CONFINED largely to NORTH + CENTRAL India. Affected areas: UP (Awadh = most intense), Delhi, Bihar, parts of MP, Rajasthan. NOT AFFECTED / LOYAL TO BRITISH: (1) PUNJAB — recently conquered (1849); Sikh soldiers actually helped British retake Delhi (memories of Mughal persecution of Gurus). (2) BENGAL PROPER — civilian areas remained largely calm. (3) SOUTH INDIA — Madras + Bombay Presidencies showed no significant rebellion. (4) MOST PRINCELY STATES — remained LOYAL: Gwalior's Scindia, Hyderabad's Nizam, Travancore, Mysore, Kashmir, Nepal (Jung Bahadur's Gurkhas HELPED British). Canning called these princes the 'BREAKWATERS IN THE STORM'. (5) MOST EDUCATED INDIANS (new middle class) — saw British as modernisers. This limited scope made the revolt defeatable. By mid-1858, British had crushed most centres. Only Tantia Tope lingered as a guerrilla till his capture + execution in April 1859.
